newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: U.S. geologist reported kidnapped in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. geologist reported kidnapped in Colombia.

text.p: A U.S. geologist was kidnapped by unidentified gunmen while working at a coal mine on Colombia's northern Guajira peninsula, authorities said on Wednesday.
Police said Frank Pescatori, a 40-year-old New Jersey man, was abducted by five gunmen early on Tuesday at a coal mining site outside the town of Hato Nuevo.

Contract workers for Geomet, Pescatori's Alabama-based mining company, watched in horror as he was bundled off by the kidnappers in a company vehicle that was later found abandoned on a nearby roadway, police sources said.
They said it was not immediately clear if the kidnappers were common criminals or leftist guerrillas operating in the area.

Colombia has the world's highest rate of kidnapping, with more than 1,150 people abducted last year alone. More than 900 have been snatched in 1996, and roughly half of the kidnappings have been blamed on guerrillas seeking to raise money for their war against the state.
